key_insight: Better non-overlapping Pauli group initializations can substantially reduce measurement cost in overlapping quantum energy estimation methods.
engineering_relevance: For variational quantum algorithms, the choice of initial grouping is an important engineering lever that can lower measurement overhead even when a downstream overlapping optimizer is used.
method: Introduce VarSI: covariance-informed non-overlapping Pauli grouping heuristics.
Use existing covariance dictionaries to guide global greedy insertion, SI-like variance-aware grouping, and local refinement.
Initialize iterative coefficient-splitting (ICS) with VarSI-generated groups to improve final measurement reduction.
evidence_signal: Across 130 molecular Hamiltonians, VarSI improved non-overlapping measurements by 38% over SI and boosted ICS results to as much as 70% reduction versus standard SI initialization.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of covariance dictionaries and qubit mapping, so gains may vary across hardware and ansatz settings.
paper_title: Reducing quantum measurements in qubit-based overlapping grouping methods for quantum energy estimation through better initializations
